title: createJevAsk cannot name its Cmd, so two Jev knobs in one machine collide
goal: `createJevAsk` accepts an optional `name` and passes it to `createResilientCall`, so each Jev knob in a machine has its own run Cmd, settle Msgs and timer Msg, typed per knob, while a knob with no name behaves exactly as it does today.

criteria.rule: One machine holding three createJevAsk knobs with three different question maps and three distinct names runs on the Effect engine, with all three calls in flight at once and a handler map that has one cell per knob and no type cast, and each answer settles into its own knob's slice with its own answer type.
criteria.no_example: This is an end-to-end machine run on the Effect engine plus a compile-time check for no cast, so it is a test fixture rather than one call with a literal result.

criteria.rule: A knob built with name "judge" has the run Cmd type "judge_run".

examples.call: createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } }, name: "judge" }).run.cmdType

criteria.rule: attempt on a knob named "judge" emits a Cmd whose type is "judge_run".

examples.call: (() => { const a = createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } }, name: "judge" }); return a.attempt(a.init(), "k", "diff", 0)[1][0].type; })()

criteria.rule: A knob named "judge" settles success as "judge_run_ok".

examples.call: createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } }, name: "judge" }).run.okType

criteria.rule: A knob named "judge" settles failure as "judge_run_err".

examples.call: createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } }, name: "judge" }).run.errType

criteria.rule: A knob named "judge" that is waiting to retry arms a timer whose Msg type is "judge_deadline".

examples.call: (() => { const a = createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } }, name: "judge", retry: { baseMs: 100, factor: 2, capMs: 1000, maxAttempts: 3, jitter: "full" } }, () => 0); const [s1, [cmd]] = a.attempt(a.init(), "k", "diff", 0); const [s2] = a.fail(s1, { type: "judge_run_err", cmd, error: { _tag: "port_rejected", jev: { _tag: "port_threw", reason: "socket" } }, at: 1 }); return a.timer(s2).msg.type; })()

criteria.rule: The knob's name field is the name it was given.

examples.call: createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } }, name: "judge" }).name

criteria.rule: A knob built without a name still has the run Cmd type "resilient_run".

examples.call: createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } } }).run.cmdType

criteria.rule: A knob built without a name still settles success as "resilient_run_ok".

examples.call: createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } } }).run.okType

criteria.rule: A knob built without a name still settles failure as "resilient_run_err".

examples.call: createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } } }).run.errType

criteria.rule: A knob built without a name that is waiting to retry still arms a timer whose Msg type is "deadline_exceeded".

examples.call: (() => { const a = createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } }, retry: { baseMs: 100, factor: 2, capMs: 1000, maxAttempts: 3, jitter: "full" } }, () => 0); const [s1, [cmd]] = a.attempt(a.init(), "k", "diff", 0); const [s2] = a.fail(s1, { type: "resilient_run_err", cmd, error: { _tag: "port_rejected", jev: { _tag: "port_threw", reason: "socket" } }, at: 1 }); return a.timer(s2).msg.type; })()

criteria.rule: When a named knob with a fallback runs out of retries, the fallback's answer settles under that knob.

examples.call: (() => { const a = createJevAsk({ questions: { fine: { type: "noul", instructions: "Is it fine?" } }, name: "judge", fallback: () => ({ fine: { type: "noul", noul: 1 } }) }); const [s1, [cmd]] = a.attempt(a.init(), "k", "diff", 0); const [s2] = a.fail(s1, { type: "judge_run_err", cmd, error: { _tag: "port_rejected", jev: { _tag: "port_threw", reason: "socket" } }, at: 1 }); return s2.calls.k.result.source; })()

title: A child stopped with run.stop() stays in the host's table under tea's spawn helper
goal: A host stops a child started with `spawn` in one call to a `stop` helper from `@demlik/tea/effect`. The host's table drops the entry and the parent is told. The examples, the how-to and the TSDoc use that helper, and none of them promises that `child.run.stop()` does the same.

criteria.rule: A host that started a parent and at least five children with `spawn` can stop three of them one by one with the `stop` helper, one of them twice and one from inside a parent Cmd handler. After each stop the host's table holds only the children still running, the parent has taken exactly one stop notice per stopped child, nothing hangs, and the host code calls no `Scope.close` on a child's scope.
criteria.no_example: This is an Effect-based scenario across several runs, with scopes, a detached notify fiber and async completion. It needs a vitest fixture (beside `packages/tea/src/effect/children.test.ts`), not one synchronous call and its return value.

criteria.rule: `@demlik/tea/effect` exports a `stop` helper from `packages/tea/src/effect/index.ts`, and the helper is defined in `packages/tea/src/effect/children.ts` beside `spawn` and `tell`.
criteria.no_example: This is about module layout and the export map. The signature is left to the build, so no fixed call and result can be written ahead of time.

criteria.rule: Stopping a child with the helper closes that child's scope. As a result its run stops, `remove` runs and takes the entry out of the host's table, and `notify` runs.
criteria.no_example: These are side effects on Effect scopes and the host's table, shown by an async Effect test, not one call's return value.

criteria.rule: Using the helper to stop a child that has already stopped succeeds and sends the parent no second notice.
criteria.no_example: This is an async Effect behavior, counted in the parent's State over time. A test in the effect test suite must show it.

criteria.rule: The helper takes and keeps no table of runs, does no lookup by id, and adds no Supervisor, registry or change stream. The host keeps its own table, ids and Msg names (#312, #556).
criteria.no_example: This limits the API shape and adds nothing a call could return. It is checked by reading `children.ts` and the helper's signature.

criteria.rule: Both `packages/tea/examples/parent-and-workers-effect.ts` (its `stop`) and `packages/tea/examples/process-tree-effect.ts` (its `stopProcess`) stop a child through the helper. Neither keeps a hand-written `Scope.close` on a child's scope.
criteria.no_example: This is a change to the source of two example files, checked by reading them. No return value shows it.

criteria.rule: `packages/tea/src/effect/many-machines-how-to.test.ts` still drives both examples and passes.
criteria.no_example: This is a test-suite outcome, not one call's value.

title: code-graph readAllowance refuses a driving adapter whose read decides nothing
goal: A hexagonal scope can list its read-only driven files in `readAllowance` without `decidedBy`, and then every driving file of that scope may import those files without B8. Writes, `application/` imports, unlisted files, and any scope that still names `decidedBy` are gated exactly as before.

criteria.rule: In a hexagonal `services/api` scope whose `readAllowance` lists four read files with no `decidedBy`, `--boundaries --ci` with no ledger exits 1 and reports exactly three B8 crossings: `ledger-http.ts` importing the unlisted `ledger-reads.ts`, `place-http.ts` importing `../../application/place`, and `ship-http.ts` importing the listed `shipment-reads.ts` that runs `UPDATE shipments SET shipped = 1`. The six clean read handlers (two each in orders, catalog and billing) produce nothing.
criteria.no_example: This is an end-to-end CLI run over a throwaway workspace (files, exit code, report rows), so no single function call and return value can show it. It belongs in a test that builds the fixture described in the issue and its amendment.

criteria.rule: In that fixture, the B8 row and the `--ci` line for `ship-http.ts` name the write: its file, its line, and the binding `DB`.
criteria.no_example: The rule is about CLI report and stdout text produced from a fixture workspace, not about a value one call returns.

criteria.rule: In that fixture, the plain `--boundaries` report and `--json` list the same three crossings and exit 0.
criteria.no_example: The rule is about CLI exit codes and output across modes over a fixture workspace.

criteria.rule: In that fixture, `--accept-crossings --reason "<why>"` writes exactly those three ledger entries, none of which carries the write site. Two further `--ci` runs then exit 0, and `boundary-ledger.json` and stdout stay byte-identical between them.
criteria.no_example: The rule is about a ledger file written to disk and byte-identical output across repeated CLI runs.

criteria.rule: In that fixture, removing the `UPDATE` from `shipment-reads.ts` makes the next `--ci` run exit 0, prune and print only the shipping entry, and leave two entries. A further run leaves the ledger byte-identical.
criteria.no_example: The rule is about editing a fixture file between CLI runs and checking the ledger file on disk.

criteria.rule: When a declared scope leaves out `decidedBy`, `readAllowanceOf` stores that scope's `decidedBy` as `null`.

examples.call: readAllowanceOf({ "services/api": { driven: ["src/orders/adapters/driven/order-reads.ts"] } }, {}).scopes.get("services/api").decidedBy

title: code-graph's wrangler config loader counts a config with a mid-file syntax error as parsed
goal: The wrangler config loader treats a .json/.jsonc config with any syntax error (other than comments, trailing commas and a leading BOM, which wrangler accepts) as unparsed, so `--boundaries` refuses on it and `--data`/`--cross-runtime` list it as UNPARSED CONFIG instead of reading a repaired object.

criteria.rule: With B17 or B18 declared, `--boundaries` (report, `--json`, `--ci`, `--accept-crossings --reason`, `--migrate-ceilings`) exits 2 with the existing one-line refusal naming only `services/auth/wrangler.jsonc` when that worker's config leaves its `d1_databases` entry unclosed before its `services` array, printing nothing on stdout and writing no `boundary-ledger.json`.
criteria.no_example: Needs the four-worker fixture workspace on disk and a CLI run checked for exit code, stdout and a ledger file; a single pure call and return value cannot show it.

criteria.rule: On the same four-worker fixture with `auth`'s entry closed, `--ci` exits 1 listing exactly two `worker-call-cycle` entries, `api, auth` and `mailer, search`; `--accept-crossings --reason` records both and two further `--ci` runs exit 0 with byte-identical stdout and `boundary-ledger.json`.
criteria.no_example: End-to-end CLI sequence over a workspace on disk, judged by exit codes and file bytes.

criteria.rule: A config wrangler accepts — a leading BOM, line and block comments, and trailing commas after the last object property and the last array element — is read as parsed and never triggers the refusal.
criteria.no_example: `loadBindingCatalog` reads config files from a repo directory on disk; the fixture needs files written first, which one expression with a literal result cannot do.

criteria.rule: `loadBindingCatalog` lists a `.json`/`.jsonc` config in `unparsedConfigs` and not in `manifests` for each of: an object left unclosed before later keys, a stray token between two properties, a missing comma between two properties, a file cut off mid-array, and an unquoted value (`"main": src/index.ts,`).
criteria.no_example: The loader reads files from disk; pinned by a table test over written fixture files, not a pure call.

criteria.rule: `loadBindingCatalog` still lists as unparsed an empty file, text that is not an object (`not a wrangler config`), and a TOML file with a syntax error.
criteria.no_example: The loader reads files from disk; pinned by rows of the same table test.

criteria.rule: The `--boundaries` refusal fires for each of the five mid-file error shapes (unclosed object, stray token, missing comma, cut off mid-array, unquoted value), one test row each.
criteria.no_example: Each row is a CLI/gate run over a workspace on disk judged by exit code.

title: code-graph boundaries: a mistyped process door like process.envv is accepted and silently enforces nothing
goal: A code-graph boundaries `doors` declaration naming a `process` member that the running Node's `process` lacks (a typo such as `process.envv`) exits 2 with a message naming the scope, the door, the nearest real member and the Node version, and writes nothing. Every real member (own or inherited, plus deeper paths below it) stays declarable without a hand-kept member list, and the lane also adds ADR 0023 for the door identity decisions and fixes #514's README and changeset nits.

criteria.rule: In a scope with features billing, users, reports and a lib folder, adding exactly one mistyped door (`process.envv`, `process.ENV` or `process.stdinn.isTTY`) to a declaration that also has the real doors `process.env`, `process.stdin.isTTY`, `process.on` and `process.hrtime.bigint` makes plain `--boundaries`, `--ci` and `--accept-crossings --reason "x"` each exit 2. Each run prints nothing on stdout, names the declared door and its nearest real member on stderr, writes no `boundary-ledger.json` and leaves an existing one byte-identical.
criteria.no_example: This is a CLI end-to-end outcome (exit codes, stdout/stderr, ledger file bytes) across three modes, so it needs the repo fixture and cannot be shown as one pure call and its return value.

criteria.rule: With only the four real doors declared and five non-owner reads present, `--boundaries --json` reports exactly 5 `door-outside-owner` entries and exits 0, and accepting them writes 5 entries that each carry the reason. After that, `--ci` exits 0 with 5 recorded crossings; a new `billing/store/audit.ts` calling `process.hrtime.bigint()` makes `--ci` exit 1 listing only that file and leaves the ledger unchanged. Once that file is accepted, removing the reads in `charge.ts` and `lib/timer.ts` makes `--ci` print `pruned 2` and leave 4 entries, and two more `--ci` runs leave the ledger byte-identical with no `pruned` line.
criteria.no_example: This is a multi-step CLI sequence over a repo fixture (exit codes, printed lines, ledger contents across repeat runs), not a single call and its return value.

criteria.rule: `doorDeclarationIssue` returns a refusal (non-null) for a declared door whose `process` member is not a property name on Node's `process`.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing", "users", "reports"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.envv": ["src/env.ts"] } } }) !== null

criteria.rule: The refusal names the scope and the declared door.

examples.call: (() => { const m = doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.envv": ["src/env.ts"] } } }); return m.includes("packages/app") && m.includes("process.envv"); })()

criteria.rule: The refusal names the nearest real member of `process`.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.envv": ["src/env.ts"] } } }).replaceAll("process.envv", "").includes("process.env")

doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.stdinn.isTTY": ["src/terminal.ts"] } } }).replaceAll("process.stdinn", "").includes("process.stdin")

criteria.rule: The nearest member is found case-insensitively, so `process.ENV` names `process.env` rather than some other three-letter member.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.ENV": ["src/env.ts"] } } }).replaceAll("process.ENV", "").includes("process.env")

criteria.rule: Ties for nearest member are broken by distance and then by name, so the same typo gives the same refusal on every run.

examples.call: (() => { const r = { features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.ENV": ["src/env.ts"] } } }; return doorDeclarationIssue(r) === doorDeclarationIssue(r); })()

criteria.rule: A member with no real member near it (`process.zzzzzzzz`) is still refused.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.zzzzzzzz": ["src/env.ts"] } } }) !== null

criteria.rule: A refusal for a member with nothing near it suggests no far-fetched member.
criteria.no_example: The issue fixes no message format or distance cutoff, so the only exact assertion would be that some text is absent from an unspecified message. The reviewer has to judge this on the refusal text.

criteria.rule: The refusal for a mistyped member names the Node version it judged against.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.envv": ["src/env.ts"] } } }).includes(process.versions.node)

criteria.rule: Real `process` members declared alongside deeper static paths under them are accepted: `process.env`, `process.stdin.isTTY`, the inherited EventEmitter method `process.on` and `process.hrtime.bigint`.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing", "users", "reports"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.env": ["src/env.ts"], "process.stdin.isTTY": ["src/terminal.ts"], "process.on": ["src/signals.ts"], "process.hrtime.bigint": ["src/clock.ts"] } } })

criteria.rule: Every string-keyed property name up `process`'s prototype chain counts as a member, so inherited EventEmitter methods such as `emit` and `once` are declarable.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.emit": ["src/signals.ts"], "process.once": ["src/signals.ts"] } } })

criteria.rule: Only the member segment is checked against Node: a segment below a real member only has to be a valid identifier, even if Node has no such property there.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.stdin.isTTYY": ["src/terminal.ts"], "process.env.CI": ["src/env.ts"] } } })

criteria.rule: The member set is collected from property names alone, without reading any values, so no getter runs (reading `process.stdin` would open a stream).
criteria.no_example: This is about a side effect (no getter is invoked while the set is built), which a call and its return value cannot show.

criteria.rule: `doors.ts` keeps no hand-written list of `process` members; the member set comes from the running Node's `process` and is passed into the check as a parameter that defaults to it.
criteria.no_example: This is about source structure and a parameter whose type the issue does not fix, so no exact call can be written for it.

criteria.rule: The door catalog still has exactly one `process.` row, the `process.<member>` family.

examples.call: DOOR_ROWS.filter((name) => name.startsWith("process."))

criteria.rule: The bare `process` is still refused as the whole family.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process": ["src/env.ts"] } } }).includes('door "process" in "packages/app" is the whole family process.<member>')

criteria.rule: A door outside the catalog is still refused as not in the door catalog.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "Math.randm": ["src/env.ts"] } } }).includes('door "Math.randm" in "packages/app" is not in the door catalog')

criteria.rule: A `doors` scope that declares no `features` is still refused.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/other": { "process.env": ["src/env.ts"] } } })
examples.result: "\"doors\" declares scope \"packages/other\", which declares no \"features\": doors ride a scope that declares features."

criteria.rule: An owner under `src/<feature>/rules/` is still refused.

examples.call: doorDeclarationIssue({ features: { "packages/app": ["billing"] }, lib: ["lib"], contracts: [], doors: { "packages/app": { "process.env": ["src/billing/rules/env.ts"] } } })
examples.result: "owner \"src/billing/rules/env.ts\" of door \"process.env\" in \"packages/app\" is under src/billing/rules/, where no door has an owner."

criteria.rule: An owner that names no file the scope loaded is still reported.

examples.call: unknownOwners({ "process.env": ["src/nope.ts"] }, new Set(["src/env.ts"]))

criteria.rule: Detection never consults the member set: a use is named for the member it read, even when Node's `process` has no such member.

examples.call: pathDoorOf(["process", "envv", "X"])

criteria.rule: The member set gates declarations only, so for the same repo every supported Node (`engines.node` >=20) produces the same ledger entry names and report bytes.
criteria.no_example: This compares output across different Node runtimes, which one call running under a single Node cannot show.

A test pins this with a stand-in member set.
criteria.no_example: The issue does not fix the shape of the member-set parameter (a Set of names, a process-like object, or something else), so no exact call can be written.

criteria.rule: A test checks that the seven names the catalog once listed row by row (`env`, `argv`, `stdin`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `exit`, `cwd`) and `on` are all in the running Node's `process`.
